title: What Should You Not Bring on a Boat Trip in Madeira?
description: Leave heels, hard luggage, glass, spray sunscreen and jewellery you love at the hotel. Food and drinks are on board, and a drone is worth asking about first.
heroAlt: Heels, glass and spray sunscreen set apart from sandals, a towel and sun cream on a pontoon
keywords: what not to bring on a boat trip in Madeira
what to leave behind on a boat trip
can I bring a drone on a boat trip Madeira
shoes for a boat trip Madeira
luggage on a boat trip Funchal

images.prompt: Top-down photograph on the weathered wooden planks of a pontoon at Marina do Funchal, Madeira, in soft morning light. On the left half, items set aside: a pair of black high heels, the handle and corner of a hard-shell suitcase, a green glass bottle and an aerosol can of sunscreen with no readable label. On the right half, what goes aboard: flat rubber sandals, a rolled striped towel, a plain tube of sun cream, sunglasses on a cord and a folded light jacket. Along the top edge of the frame, the edge of a white boat hull with a grey cushioned seat. Realistic, true colours, no text, no logos, no people.
images.alt: Heels, glass and spray sunscreen set apart from sandals, a towel and sun cream on a pontoon

images.prompt: Bare feet seen from behind walking carefully across the wet white deck of a motor boat after a swim, a damp towel hanging over a grey cushioned seat, late morning sun off Madeira's south coast, no faces.
images.alt: Bare feet on a wet boat deck after the swim stop

images.prompt: A straw hat with a chin strap and a pair of sunglasses on a cord resting on a grey cushioned seat of a white motor boat, the green and brown cliffs west of Funchal soft in the background, bright midday light.
images.alt: A hat with a chin strap and sunglasses on a cord on a boat seat
